A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DNO/PRNO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy diffusion simulations, image-reward optimization experiments, regularization comparisons and appendix analyses. Some baseline statistics are explicitly borrowed from prior papers.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulations, image-generation experiments and appendix analyses, including the authors' DNO/PRNO and hybrid-gradient results.

M1.justification: DNO, probability regularization, SDE noise optimization and Hybrid-1/Hybrid-2 retain their procedures and objectives. The added DDIM pseudocode, update equations and vector-Jacobian explanation document existing components rather than introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both retain the toy distributions, SD v1.5 brightness and human-feedback reward tasks, JPEG optimization and SDXL examples. The new API discussion explains the existing black-box Aesthetic Score experiment; it does not add an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SD v1.5, LGD, SPIN, DDPO and AlignProp. Section 5.3 still compares ZO-SGD, Hybrid-1 and Hybrid-2. Newly cited works are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The sampling settings, metrics, optimization budgets and Appendix D hyperparameters remain unchanged, including 50-step DDIM and gradient-estimation sample counts of 16, 8 and 4. The newly stated toy learning rate is additional documentation, not a revision of a previously reported setting.

E4.justification: The ODE/SDE comparison, regularization experiments, gradient-estimator comparison, qualitative examples, probability-indicator investigations and k/b/gamma sensitivity analyses are retained. The added mathematical SDE discussion supplies no new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that figure results use 1,000 random seeds and report means with standard deviations. The uncertainty bands and the practice of plotting best-so-far ZO-SGD rewards are retained.

E6.justification: Table 1 is numerically identical, including 10-minute PRNO scores of 10.68 for Aesthetic, 0.354 for HPS and 25.16 for PickScore. Matched experimental curves and qualitative examples, including all appendices, retain their results; the modified plots only add axis labels.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Eqs. (12)–(13), expressing ODE sampling through deterministic SDE noise and comparing optimal attainable rewards. This extends the formal sampler comparison locally; Theorem 1, the concentration bounds and Appendix B's proof and stationary-point cases remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about tuning-free alignment, probability regularization, non-differentiable rewards and competitive reward scores. The new explanation of the unchanged sampling map clarifies the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v1 motivates SDE optimization through observed speed and finer control. v2 adds a feasible-set interpretation and extrapolates its optimal-value inequality to an assertion that SDE optimization will perform at least as well. It also expands the rationale for API-only rewards; existing reward-hacking explanations and latency limitations remain.

D1.justification: The promise of future code is replaced by an Official Implementation repository link. v2 adds DDIM pseudocode and discloses the toy experiment's 0.01 learning rate. Appendix D's checkpointing, optimizer, perturbation and hardware details are retained; repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sun et al. (2022) and Lin et al. (2024) to motivate black-box rewards and more explicitly distinguishes DNO from methods that modify the sampling map. The duplicated Wang et al. reference represents a work already present in v1, not another distinct addition.

P1.justification: The method exposition is substantially expanded across Sections 1.1.2, 2 and 4, with a DDIM walkthrough, explicit optimization explanations and fuller black-box reward motivation. Numerous passages are rewritten while the section hierarchy remains. Section 2.1 also introduces a duplicated explanation following Theorem 1.

P2.justification: v2 adds conceptual and computational diagrams as Figures 2–3 and a boxed DDIM algorithm. Several captions become more informative, and Figures 9–10 gain steps labels. Existing empirical graphics and Table 1's structure are retained, with figures reflowed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new diagrams, fuller method explanations, toy learning-rate disclosure and implementation link make the retained work easier to understand and reproduce. These provide a limited overall benefit. The additions also introduce duplicated prose and an overstatement in Section 2.2: comparing global optima does not establish faster convergence or uniformly better outcomes from actual optimization.
